description: Disable all password-based SSH authentication methods (PasswordAuthentication, KbdInteractiveAuthentication) in sshd, requiring public key authentication exclusively. This eliminates the entire password attack surface for SSH — brute force, credential stuffing, and dictionary attacks become impossible regardless of password strength or lockout policy. Supported key types include Ed25519 (recommended), ECDSA, and RSA (4096-bit minimum). Both PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication must be set to 'no' — disabling only PasswordAuthentication leaves keyboard-interactive password prompts active on many configurations. On RHEL 9+, the AuthenticationMethods directive can further restrict to publickey-only. Key management (rotation, passphrase protection, authorized_keys auditing) becomes the primary credential risk surface. Does not protect against pre-authentication SSH daemon vulnerabilities or key compromise via stolen private keys.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: With password authentication enabled, attackers use standard brute-force tools (Hydra, Medusa) against SSH with publicly available credential dumps — attack complexity is Low. With key-only authentication, the attacker must obtain the target's private key through a separate compromise: stealing from a developer workstation, extracting from CI/CD secrets, compromising a jump host with agent forwarding, or insider access. Each path requires a multi-step attack chain with preconditions that raise complexity from trivial credential guessing to targeted key theft

verification.method: Verify all password-based SSH authentication methods are disabled and only public key authentication is accepted

remediation.name: sshd key-only authentication via drop-in config

steps.description: Create an sshd drop-in config that disables all password-based authentication and enforces public key only. Both PasswordAuthentication and KbdInteractiveAuthentication must be disabled — disabling only PasswordAuthentication leaves keyboard-interactive password prompts active on many configurations
steps.command:
printf 'PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
AuthenticationMethods publickey
' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-cme-804-key-only.conf

steps.description: Validate sshd configuration before restarting to avoid lockout from syntax errors
Restart sshd to apply the new authentication policy
Set PasswordAuthentication to no in the Windows OpenSSH server config
Ensure PubkeyAuthentication is enabled in the Windows OpenSSH server config
Restart the Windows OpenSSH server service to apply changes
